title: One ecosystem. A clearer story.
description: Website redesign and product dashboards that connect Nerdma’s governance, risk and sustainability offer.

details.context: Nerdma Systems · Governance, risk and sustainability intelligence

sections.title: The challenge
paragraphs: Five named products were presented separately, leaving technical evaluators and decision-makers to work out how the ecosystem fitted together. Credibility and the path to enquiry needed to be easier to find.

sections.title: The approach
paragraphs: Audit the content and competing platforms, map the buyer’s decision, then organise the site around problem, product and proof. Give every product a stated role and bring certifications, partners and clients into the main story.

sections.title: From website to product
paragraphs: Design NerdScore, NerdGrid and NerdGrow dashboards with a shared reading order: the primary number, its trend, then contributing factors. Use consistent tables and filters across the interfaces.

sections.title: Delivery & evidence
paragraphs: The original project documents content structure, responsive design/build, forms and analytics. The live website is linked below. No measured before-and-after enquiry or ranking improvement is claimed.

title: From messages to a structured food order.
description: An ordering PWA designed around a local kitchen, a clear menu and an easier path to reorder.

sections.title: The problem
paragraphs: Direct-message ordering makes it easy to miss an item or an order detail. The design brief was to create a structured path from choosing food to placing an order, without making a small kitchen’s work harder.

sections.title: The product approach
paragraphs: Organise the menu around how customers browse, make item choices and basket contents explicit, and bring the reorder path forward. Treat a phone as the primary screen for customers and kitchen updates.

sections.title: Design & delivery
paragraphs: The original portfolio documents product design and an end-to-end PWA build. The public ordering flow can be explored through the live site.

sections.title: Evidence & next questions
paragraphs: The project notes describe funnel instrumentation but do not supply a measured before-and-after comparison. Order accuracy and the share of repeat orders are useful next validation questions—not published outcomes.

title: A shared path from brief to handoff.
description: A role-based product workspace connecting business, design, development, quality and delivery.

details.context: Product operations · High-level product-design case study

sections.title: The product problem
paragraphs: Product intent gets fragmented as it moves between business, design, engineering, quality and delivery. ProdOps explores a workspace where each role can see its own process while keeping a shared brief and explicit handoffs.

sections.title: The design response
paragraphs: Use an IDE-like layout: role navigation, numbered steps and files, a central editor, and contextual assistance. Separate role-specific deliverables from read-only upstream context so a team can see where decisions came from.

sections.title: Key product decisions
paragraphs: Make approvals visible, with notes and a revisit state when upstream work changes. These are local workflow aids—not multi-user permissions.
Connect scope, requirements, design, tests and handoff through editable documents and traceability views. Keep export packs available so the work can continue in an external development environment.
Let manual editing and exports work without an AI provider. Clearly separate browser-only functionality from server-dependent drafting and imports.

sections.title: What is implemented
paragraphs: The README describes browser-based editing, saved projects, role workflows, approvals, exports and the ProdOps Lab. A static preview is published on GitHub Pages. AI drafting and reference imports require an appropriately configured server; framework compilation and production delivery happen outside this workspace.

sections.title: Status & next validation
paragraphs: This is an in-progress product documented from its README, not a claimed adoption success. Test whether users can follow an end-to-end brief-to-handoff journey, identify missing dependencies and recover from changed decisions before drawing usability or delivery-speed conclusions.

gallery.caption: Actual local build of the public ProdOps repository, showing its supplied worked example.

title: One design language, across the stack.
description: A work-in-progress design-to-code system connecting Figma, typed tokens, React, Angular and Storybook.

sections.title: The challenge
paragraphs: Keep design decisions consistent between a Figma workflow, typed design tokens and framework-specific components—without pretending the design system is complete or adoption-validated.

sections.title: The approach
paragraphs: Connect Figma decisions to token generation, shared React and Angular libraries, and Storybook verification. Keep plugin work local-first and make review and accessibility checks part of handoff.

sections.title: Product decisions
paragraphs: Use one shared token source, make component variants inspectable, and expose token aliases and selected contrast checks through Review Lab. Keep local snapshots separate from shared team history.

sections.title: Current boundaries
paragraphs: The original portfolio describes the plugin as awaiting Figma Community review. Its illustrations are diagrams rather than captured product screens. Wider interaction coverage, native-library sharing and production adoption remain work in progress.
